title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for colon cancer and assessment of treatment side effects.

HPI
The patient is a 74-year-old woman presenting for a routine follow-up regarding her diagnosis of colon carcinoma. She is currently receiving chemotherapy for the malignant neoplasm. She reports that she has been feeling generally well, though she notes some mild fatigue and occasional nausea following her recent infusions. She denies any significant abdominal pain, changes in bowel habits, or unintentional weight loss at this time. She states that the treatment is continuing as scheduled and she is compliant with all prescribed medications. She is here today to monitor her tolerance to the current regimen.

Review of Systems
The patient reports no fevers, chills, or night sweats. She denies any shortness of breath or chest pain. She reports mild fatigue but denies significant muscle weakness. She denies any new-onset rashes or joint pain. Appetite is stable. No reports of palpitations or dizziness.

Social History
The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is a retired teacher and enjoys gardening and walking. She denies any tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother had hypertension. Father had type 2 diabetes. Siblings are healthy.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on room air
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 4.5 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 160 x 10^9/L
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
eGFR: 78 mL/min/1.73m2

Medication List
Metformin 500mg BID
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Ondansetron 8mg as needed for nausea

Exam
General: The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress.
Abdomen: Soft, non-distended, and non-tender to palpation. No masses or guarding noted.
Musculoskeletal: No significant edema or erythema in lower extremities.

Assessment
The patient is a 74-year-old woman with colon carcinoma who is currently receiving chemotherapy. She is tolerating the treatment well with manageable side effects.

Plan
1. Continue current chemotherapy regimen as prescribed by the oncology team.
2. Continue current medications for hypertension and diabetes.
3. Monitor CBC and metabolic panels every 4 weeks.
4. Patient to call the office if she experiences severe nausea or fever.

Electronically signed, A. Rivera, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the colon under current treatment is a current malignancy: C18.9.

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
